title: Rich & Fudgy 5-Minute Microwave Mug Brownie for Late-Night Cravings
description: Cure your late-night chocolate craving in minutes. This fudgy microwave mug brownie is rich, gooey, and made with simple pantry staples.
story: It was pouring rain against my apartment window last Tuesday around 9:30 PM, the kind of dreary night where you just want chocolate and zero dirty pans. I put on my mellow indie folk playlist, padded over to the kitchen in wool socks, and opened the pantry. I didn't want to preheat a giant oven and wait forty minutes just for a single square of dessert. Early on when testing mug bakes, I made the rookie mistake of adding a whole egg—it turned out like a rubbery chocolate omelet. Leaving out the egg entirely and trusting melted Kerrygold butter and a splash of whole milk was the turning point. This little mug bake gives you that deeply crackled, gooey center with molten pockets of chocolate in barely five minutes flat. It saved my sweet tooth and felt like an instant hug in ceramic form.
ingredients: 1 tablespoon packed light brown sugar (adds moisture)
2 tablespoons Dutch-process cocoa powder (like Hershey's Special Dark)
Pinch of Diamond Crystal kosher salt
2 tablespoons melted Kerrygold unsalted butter (or neutral oil)
2 tablespoons semi-sweet chocolate chips (plus a few extra for the top)
instructions: Grab an 8 to 10-ounce microwave-safe ceramic mug. Add your flour, granulated sugar, brown sugar, cocoa powder, and that pinch of kosher salt directly inside. Take a tiny fork or mini whisk and fluff everything together until no dry cocoa clumps remain.

Pour in the melted butter, room-temperature milk, and vanilla extract. Stir gently from the bottom up until a thick, glossy chocolate batter forms. Be careful not to whip it aggressively—just stir until the flour streaks disappear so it stays tender.
Fold in the chocolate chips, pressing a couple directly into the center so they turn into a molten pocket while cooking. Scatter two or three extra chips over the top surface.

Microwave on high (1000W) for 55 to 65 seconds. The top should look just set along the edges with a soft, slightly glistening center. Let it rest for a full 2 minutes so the carryover steam finishes cooking the crumb without drying it out.
proHack: Do not skip the 2-minute resting window right after cooking. Microwave desserts continue baking from internal steam after the timer dings. If you eat it instantly, it feels slightly wet; if you microwave it longer thinking it looks undone, it turns to rubber. 60 seconds cook time plus 2 minutes rest equals pure fudgy heaven.
storage: Honestly, this is designed as a single-serve treat eaten straight from the mug! But if you can't finish it, cover the mug tightly with foil or plastic wrap and keep it on the counter for up to 12 hours. Just pop it back into the microwave for 10 seconds with a teaspoon of milk drizzled over the top to bring back that glossy, warm texture.

faqs.question: Can I substitute the whole milk if I don't have it?
faqs.answer: Yes, absolutely! Creamy oat milk (like Oatly) works amazingly well and keeps it super rich. Unsweetened almond milk or even brewed room-temperature coffee (if you want a deep mocha vibe) make great swaps.

faqs.question: How do I prevent the mug brownie from getting dry or spongy?
faqs.answer: Never add an egg to a single-mug brownie recipe—there's just too much liquid and protein for that amount of flour, which creates a sponge-cake texture. Also, keep your cook time capped at 60 seconds; overcooking by even 15 seconds will evaporate the moisture.
